## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the docs in scope traces to the rule text, the factor ladders, the compute chains (for precision such as "latest retirement … of any reason", "no payment method", "including the dividend being reversed") or the variant parameters. No added confirmation, review, notification, wait or step was found. Specific checks:
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none. Each tool name appears only in its own policy's platform block (mechanical scan over all of `docs/`).
- A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact: none; all worked figures are labelled hypothetical. Observation only: the hypothetical worked line in `amount_counted_against_quarter` uses a purchase "dated 20 May 2026" and `reversal_holding_period_fraction` works the date "20 May 2026 → 42", which coincide with task 0's purchase date; amounts differ and the lines are labelled hypothetical, so this is not a world-state fact.

Policy-side note (not a KB defect): `dividend_and_preferred_purchase_terms` row "Which shares earn a quarter's dividend — Average daily shares held in the quarter" faithfully renders the surviving variant parameter `dividend_record_rule: average daily shares held in the quarter`, while the source retires the clause using it and computes the dividend on quarter-end shares with a latest-entry day adjustment. The KB carries both exactly as the source has them (the circular marks the clause retired; the declaration doc states the current basis), so the reader is not left with two equal formulas; the residue originates in the source's parameter set.

Policy-side note: `shares_counted_toward_ceiling` carries the source's rationale "because the ceiling governs what a member buys"; the source applies that factor only to the holding-ceiling excess, and the KB keeps the distinct terms ("shares counted toward the ceiling" vs "present shares"), which is what lets the reader keep it off the purchase room.
